title: Usage slab sawtooth prototype notes
content:
Purpose
- quick brain-dump for a slabed / sawtooth usage billing idea: give repeated micro-credits in slabs that re-fill on slower cadence to encourage steady usage and penalize bursts. target: interactive apps with lots of tiny calls + occasional long generations.

Design sketch (high-level)
- Users get a base monthly allocation of 'micro-slabs' (MS). Each MS = 500 tokens of immediate-budget. Slabs refill on a staggered schedule: 25% every 6 hours (=> full refill in 24h). Extra bursts draw from a payg reservoir.
- Sawtooth effect: short bursts are absorbed by available MS; long sustained high-throughput forces payg or escalates to higher slab tier. This smooths variance for us and signals heavy users to commit.

Why this could help (hypotheses)
- Reduces tiny-call overhead on metering (grouping many tiny calls into a slab amortization).
- More predictable token burn pattern across day (less spikes).
- Converts transient heavy users into commit candidates because sustained use rapidly consumes payg reservoir and is visible.

Unit-econ back-of-envelope
Assumptions (conservative):
- GPU cost (amortized infra + hosting + overhead) = $1.20 per 1M tokens for mixed gen/embedding workload (approx from infra bucket A).
- infra + support + fixed = $0.30 per 1M tokens => total cost = $1.50 / 1M tokens.
- Target gross margin = 60% => price should be ~$3.75 / 1M tokens.

Mapping to slabs:
- 1 MS = 500 tokens => cost_to_us = 500 * (1.50/1e6) = $0.00075 per MS.
- If we price MS effectively as 500 tokens at $3.75/1M => retail MS = 500 * (3.75/1e6) = $0.001875 => margin per MS ~ 60%.
- Monthly base package = 12,000 MS (6M tokens) => retail = 6 * $3.75 = $22.5; cost_to_us = 6 * $1.5 = $9 => gross margin ~ 60% (matches target).

Sawtooth tiers (sketch)
- Free: 200 MS/mo, refill 50% daily (encourage exploration; heavy usage forced to payg)
- Starter: 12k MS/mo (~6M tokens), refill 25% every 6h, payg throttle at 1.2x baseline price
- Mid: 60k MS/mo (~30M tokens), higher refill (faster) and lower payg premium
- Enterprise: custom refill curves, reserve-burst pools, SLA-backed latency + capacity

Example user behavior (toy scenarios)
1) Chatbot with 40 short turns/day (avg 120 tokens out & 300 tokens in) => ~16800 tokens/day = 504k tokens/mo -> ~1008 MS/mo => fits in Starter with cushion. Nice predictable revenue.
2) Burst app: many small calls for sign-in checks (20k calls/day * 40 tokens = 800k tokens/day) => 24M tokens/mo ~ 48k MS => would push Starter user into payg or require Mid tier. Sawtooth refill forces either commit or payg.

Edge cases & considerations
- Metering precision: avoid per-call overhead by charging at slab resolution (round up to nearest MS) but add a smoothing window (10s) to coalesce calls from same session to avoid penalizing chat UI with many tiny pings.
- Abuse: cheap micro-slabs could be gamed to do high qps; rate-limit per-user QPS and require identity verification for scale.
- Accounting: show users MS balance + expected refill schedule in console; show 'time-to-refill' countdown to reduce surprises.

Rollout plan (quick)
- A/B test with 5% of new Starter cohort: track conversion to commit, average daily token smoothness, and backfill to payg.
- Metrics: churn, commit rate, avg tokens/day per active user, payg revenue lift, infra spike frequency.

Questions to resolve
- How to map embeddings (expensive per token) vs. gen tokens? potentially weight MS differently (e.g., 1 embedding token = 2 MS).
- Is staggered refill 25%/6h optimal? try 12h/50% vs 6h/25% in experiments.
- UI clarity: how to present refill without confusing users (visual vs billing explanation).

Notes / To-do
- Build small sim: synthetic user classes (low, medium, bursty) and run month with different refill schedules to see payg uplift and infra smoothing.
- Talk to infra cost team to validate $/1M tokens estimate for our current mixes.
- Quick mock of console balance view for PM review.

Random scribbles
- Could create a "slab swap" for teams: allow converting unused slabs at month-end to infra credits or partner credits at 10% value; helps retention.
- Consider "session bundling": N slabs reserved per active session to guarantee low-latency bursts (good for VOIP/agent usecases).

End of pad (for now).
